$comment: Authoritative inventory of the 11 prior real-SQLite concurrency cases, reconstructed from the disposable harness lib/services/meetingRegister/__tests__/realSqliteConcurrency.test.ts and the isolated evidence targeted-real-sqlite-isolated.txt (SHA256 6e12a75345a7f89ab3ae5909763d70b599b251b8b9f1a98c97fb4c72435f6e25). 'match' is the unique Vitest -t fragment used to run each case in its own process.

cases.area: meeting materialization vs source ownership serialization
cases.behavior: A history-materialization transaction that begins first must durably commit; a separate-client source (transcript) claim that starts while history holds the write must lose as a normalized frozen/conflict outcome, never partially mutating the source pointer.
cases.competingOps: Client A $transaction: meetingHistoryMaterializationGate + meetingRegisterEntry.create (held on a deferred barrier). Concurrently withMutableMeetingTranscript() attempting meeting.update(status=UPLOADING).
cases.coordination: The history transaction resolves an in-process barrier only after real lock acquisition. The source claim then starts while that lock is held; a timer only releases the established lock and is not the race-entry primitive.
cases.expectedLoser: source claim resolves { ok:false, reason:'frozen' } with no status change.
cases.auditHistory: Register entry durably present; a subsequent source claim still returns frozen.
cases.retryConflict: Frozen is terminal for this meeting; no retry succeeds.

cases.area: attachment/blob source-ownership vs the five protected history writers
cases.behavior: When the source (upload) owns the meeting (UPLOADING), every one of the five protected history writers must be refused with source-mutation and write zero rows.
cases.competingOps: Sequential withMeetingHistoryMaterialization() attempts across MeetingTranscriptSegment, MeetingTranscriptCorrection, MeetingRegisterEntry, MeetingExtractionRun, MeetingMinutesRevision.
cases.coordination: Durable-state handoff: UPLOADING is committed before each protected writer. This case proves conflict serialization, not live overlap.
cases.expectedLoser: all five writers return { ok:false, reason:'source-mutation' }.
cases.auditHistory: No protected history row created while source owns the meeting.
cases.retryConflict: Each writer independently refused; no partial write.

cases.area: lease ownership — concurrent CAS source claim (duplicate processing prevention)
cases.behavior: Two concurrent compare-and-set source claims must yield exactly one winner (updateMany count 1) and one loser (count 0), with no torn state.
cases.competingOps: Promise.all of two withMutableMeetingTranscript() claims, each meeting.updateMany(where status in [PENDING,FAILED]) -> UPLOADING with a distinct marker.
cases.coordination: Both claims are created without awaiting either operation, then Promise.all observes the two concurrent CAS results.
cases.retryConflict: CAS predicate makes the second claim a clean no-op, not an error.

cases.area: raw engine contention control — SQLITE_BUSY/timeout without partial commit
cases.behavior: A raw separate-client write contending with a held write transaction must EITHER wait and commit OR fail with busy/locked/timeout — in both branches leaving no partial commit. This is the engine control proving the failure mode exists outside the normalization wrappers.
cases.competingOps: Client A $transaction holds meeting.update(audioFileName=holder.wav) on a barrier; Client B raw meeting.update(audioStorageKey=contender.wav).
cases.coordination: The holder resolves an in-process barrier only after real lock acquisition. The contender then starts while that lock is held; a timer only releases the established lock and is not the race-entry primitive.
cases.expectedLoser: contender either commits audioStorageKey after waiting, or errors busy/locked/transaction and leaves audioStorageKey NULL.
cases.expectedRows: audioFileName=holder.wav; historyCounts=[0,0,0,0,0]; no partial mutation in either branch.
cases.retryConflict: Engine-level busy is intentionally surfaced here (NOT normalized to 409); its two valid branches are engine-nondeterministic and excluded from the deterministic evidence hash.

cases.area: stale lease recovery — ownership lost before commit (transaction conflict)
cases.behavior: If ownership is lost (state moved off UPLOADING) before the guarded mutation commits, withActiveMeetingTranscriptMutation must return state-conflict and leave the source pointer unchanged.
cases.competingOps: Client B moves meeting.status UPLOADING->READY, then withActiveMeetingTranscriptMutation(expected=UPLOADING) attempts meeting.update(audioStorageKey).
cases.coordination: Durable-state handoff: READY commits before the stale-owner mutation. This case proves deterministic stale-lease conflict, not live overlap.
cases.dbState: meeting.status begins UPLOADING, mutated to READY by the racing client.
cases.retryConflict: State-conflict is deterministic via the expected-state CAS predicate.

cases.area: concurrent BackgroundJob claim — duplicate active-slot prevention + slot reuse after failure
cases.behavior: Two simultaneously released createJob reservations must produce exactly one active-slot winner and one uniqueness loser; after failJob releases the winning slot, the losing logical operation can retry with a new id.
cases.competingOps: Two armed createJob(meeting_transcription) reservations launch from one shared start barrier; failJob(winner) releases the slot; createJob(retry) reserves it.
cases.coordination: Both reservation functions report armed before the shared barrier releases either operation. Exactly one captured result must succeed and one must carry the expected P2002/unique active-slot result.
cases.dbState: No active BackgroundJob before the shared release.
cases.expectedWinner: exactly one simultaneous reservation holds activeSlot=1.
cases.expectedLoser: exactly one simultaneous reservation returns the expected uniqueness/active-slot error.
cases.expectedRows: After failJob and retry: the winner is failed with activeSlot=NULL; the distinct retry is queued with activeSlot=1; exactly two job rows exist.
cases.retryConflict: Active-slot uniqueness enforces single ownership; retry allowed only post-release.

cases.area: duplicate processing prevention / media job idempotency — failJob under contention
cases.behavior: failJob under a held row lock must converge to a durable failed row and be idempotent: status=failed, activeSlot=null, externalJobId preserved, and a repeat failJob leaves the same terminal row.
cases.competingOps: Client A $transaction holds backgroundJob.update on a barrier; failJob(job,'injected',providerId) contends; then a second identical failJob.
cases.coordination: A child-process IPC barrier proves the BackgroundJob write lock is held. The real failJob must enqueue exactly one retry timer before release; only then is the lock released and the observed timer advanced.
cases.expectedWinner: failJob commits after the lock releases.
cases.expectedLoser: no torn row; the lock holder's write is preserved until release.
cases.expectedRows: backgroundJob = { status:'failed', activeSlot:null, externalJobId:'provider-injected' } after both calls.
cases.auditHistory: Idempotent terminal reconciliation; provider id retained.
cases.retryConflict: Real bounded contention-retry entry is asserted through the observable backoff timer; the second failJob is a durable no-op.

cases.match: reconciles provider id and releases active slot
cases.area: media job idempotency — provider-id reconciliation after ownership loss
cases.behavior: When arming the provider loses ownership (state-conflict), the job must still reconcile to failed with the provider id recorded and the active slot released.
cases.competingOps: createJob(related=meeting); racing status UPLOADING->READY; withActiveMeetingTranscriptMutation arming TRANSCRIBING fails state-conflict; failJob(job,'ownership lost',providerId).
cases.coordination: Durable-state handoff: READY commits before the stale-owner arm attempt, followed by terminal reconciliation. This case proves conflict convergence, not live overlap.
cases.dbState: meeting UPLOADING with a related job; racing client sets READY.
cases.expectedLoser: arm returns state-conflict; provider never armed.
cases.auditHistory: Provider id reconciled onto the terminal failed row.
cases.retryConflict: Deterministic state-conflict then durable failure convergence.

cases.area: attachment/blob-reference safety — real upload route durable-reservation failure
cases.behavior: The REAL upload route must return 503 before any provider egress when the durable BackgroundJob reservation fails, must not delete the prior referenced blob, must not create a new referenced blob, and must mark the meeting FAILED.
cases.competingOps: Pre-existing active job consumes the slot; real uploadPOST() with a new audio file while a prior referenced blob exists.
cases.coordination: Durable uniqueness handoff: the active-slot row and referenced blob are committed before the route executes, deterministically forcing pre-egress reservation failure.
cases.dbState: PENDING meeting with an existing audioStorageKey referenced blob and an active job holding the slot.
cases.expectedWinner: the pre-existing referenced blob and pointer survive.
cases.expectedLoser: the upload reservation fails; response.status=503; fetch never called.
cases.expectedRows: meeting.status=FAILED; storage dir still contains only old-referenced.wav; prior bytes intact.
cases.auditHistory: Exactly two persisted AuditEvent rows are asserted in order: transcription_upload_started then transcription_failed, with failureClass=job-tracking and blobCleanupFailed=false.
cases.retryConflict: 503 is the retryable contract; no provider call, no blob loss.

cases.area: Consultant/analysis transaction conflict — analyze route ownership failure
cases.behavior: The REAL analyze route must return 409 before provider egress when analysis ownership cannot be taken, leaving the meeting state unchanged.
cases.competingOps: Real analyzePOST() against a meeting already owned by the source path (UPLOADING).
cases.coordination: Durable ownership handoff: UPLOADING commits before the route executes, deterministically forcing the pre-egress conflict.
cases.dbState: meeting.status=UPLOADING with a confidential transcript present.
cases.expectedRows: meeting.status stays UPLOADING; no provider egress.
cases.auditHistory: No analysis run created; confidential transcript never leaves via provider.
cases.retryConflict: 409 is the retryable conflict contract before any egress.

cases.area: retry after the losing transaction / terminal reconciliation — provider id preserved
cases.behavior: A successful provider linkage (startJob) must set running/activeSlot=1/externalJobId, and a subsequent terminal failJob for a reconciliation failure must preserve the provider id while releasing the slot.
cases.coordination: Ordered lifecycle handoff across committed queued, running, and failed states. This reconciliation case is sequential and does not claim live overlap.
cases.expectedWinner: running state with activeSlot=1 and externalJobId=provider-running.
cases.expectedLoser: terminal failJob converges to failed while keeping the provider id.
cases.auditHistory: Provider id preserved across the running->failed terminal reconciliation.
cases.retryConflict: Terminal reconciliation is idempotent and slot-releasing.
